rationale: These 20 OSV IDs are known function-level-reachable vulnerabilities in transitive dependencies. They were ADVISORY exit-0 on every model-gateway build until this audit. The baseline + delta gate prevents NEW vulnerabilities from being introduced silently. The 20 entries themselves are explicit debts marked for remediation via Go module upgrade in a separate PR.
remediation_path: Upgrade golang.org/x/crypto, golang.org/x/net, golang.org/x/sys to versions >= fixed_version listed below. Run go mod tidy; re-run govulncheck; expected post-upgrade count: 0.
remediation_owner: chora-model-gateway maintainer (M15.5 follow-up CHO ticket — to be filed)

gate_semantics.fail_on: Any OSV ID found by govulncheck that is NOT in baseline_osvs[].id
gate_semantics.pass_on: Empty findings, OR findings whose OSV IDs are all in baseline_osvs[].id (even if count of finding records changes)
gate_semantics.advisory_on: Unused baseline_osvs entries (OSVs in baseline but not in current scan) — log only, do not fail

baseline_osvs.fixed_version: none (openpgp package deprecated wholesale; advisory has introduced=0 and no fix event)
baseline_osvs.summary: x/crypto/openpgp unmaintained/unsafe-by-design advisory. Module-level require only: govulncheck symbol analysis shows zero call paths from model-gateway (verified in-container 2026-07-27, CHO-2371). No upgrade clears it; remediation is dropping the transitive requirement, tracked with the baseline's existing x/crypto debt.
